particularites.text: Heineken N.V. is controlled through a dual-listed structure: Heineken Holding N.V. (separately listed in Amsterdam under HEIO.AS) holds 50,0% of the capital of Heineken N.V. and is itself controlled at ~52,6% by L'Arche Green N.V., the vehicle of the Heineken family (Charlene de Carvalho-Heineken) - a durable family control despite a minority direct economic holding in the listed stock itself, a structure identical every year and not tied to a one-off event.

ownership.insiderDesc: Heineken Holding N.V. (separately listed in Amsterdam under HEIO.AS), holder of 50,0% of the capital of Heineken N.V. and itself controlled at ~52,6% by L'Arche Green N.V., the control vehicle of the Heineken family (Charlene de Carvalho-Heineken). FEMSA (Mexican beverage group) separately holds ~14,8% of the capital of Heineken N.V., a strategic stake inherited from the 2010 Heineken-FEMSA agreement, reinforced since 2023 by a reciprocal cross-holding mechanism with Heineken Holding N.V. (cross dividends mutually waived on the shares held, see note 10 to the H1 2026 accounts).

clesRetenues: Q Edward Mundy (Jefferies) - what are the two or three key factors behind the success of EverGreen 2030, must the new management maintain strategic continuity, why not narrow the guidance despite the H1 beat: Harold van den Broek (CFO) identifies three differentiators - deliberate focus on fewer markets and powerful brands, building global scale by leaning on local capabilities through AI and digital, faster organisational execution; keeps the guidance range because of persistent macroeconomic/geopolitical uncertainty and the risk that the festive-season rebound in Vietnam does not repeat in the same way.

Q Sanjeet Aujla (UBS) - what investment is needed for the recovery of the Americas (marketing, route-to-market, pricing), why are European margins not stronger despite the productivity gains: van den Broek explains that the difficulties in the Americas stem from past pricing actions requiring a recalibration, cites the promising launch of Heineken Ultimate 3.5%; on Europe, specifies that he prioritises regaining market and category share rather than immediate profit, citing an unfavourable channel mix (off-trade growing, on-trade lagging) and deliberate brand-activation investment below price inflation.

Q Laurence Whyatt (Barclays) - is double-digit growth in China sustainable given the decline of the overall beer market, what are the prospects for Heineken 0.0 Ultimate: van den Broek says he is confident in sustainable growth 'for a few years' thanks to distribution gains and rising velocity, noting that 30% of the Heineken brand's distribution remains under-penetrated; on 0.0 Ultimate, he emphasises broadening consumption occasions along different articulations by market, and says it is still too early to be precise about what is working.

Q Olivier Nicolai (Goldman Sachs) - what share of head-office costs is transitory, how to restore market share in Mexico, what growth potential for Murphy's in the United Kingdom: van den Broek describes head-office costs as 'transitory in nature', tied to the build-out of the new EverGreen model, and suggests contacting IR for the detail; for Mexico, he details the expansion of the SIX store network, the strengthening of the portfolio and regional geographic diversification; on Murphy's, he highlights the 'fantastic proposition' with the launch of nitro cans and a broader expansion of the brand, notably in Ireland.

Q Chris Pitcher (Rothschild & Co Redburn) - how will the costs tied to the Middle East crisis propagate into H2 in South-East Asia/India, can the margin grow in H2, should India redirect away from contract manufacturing: van den Broek acknowledges that government support cushioned the first-half impact but warns that 'the first half is not representative' of what follows, with a lag in the pass-through of costs; defends the partnership manufacturing model as 'well governed and long term', describing a network optimisation rather than a strategic change.

Q Simon Hales (Citi) - is the market share momentum in Vietnam sustainable in H2, what explains the outperformance of Star Pubs: van den Broek tempers expectations, noting that the '6% market growth' and the 'record market shares' benefited from festive seasonality, and expects 'not to see numbers in the twenties again' in H2; for Star Pubs, he credits more than 200 M€ of investment in the estate, the premium positioning of the portfolio, an active pub acquisition/disposal strategy and a full execution/upgrade.

Q Richard Withagen (Kepler) - where are functional beers strongest and how do they differentiate themselves, why such a sudden improvement in free cash-flow: van den Broek explains that functional beer trends differ by market (health benefits meaning different things depending on the region), with opportunities in hydration, flavours and reduced-alcohol propositions; on cash-flow, he credits two factors - lower capital requirements through smarter phasing and an optimisation of inventories/payments of around four days on average, 'with more to come'.

Q Javier Gonzalez Lastra (Berenberg) - which geographies saw the 3000 headcount reductions, will H2 show a better conversion of the savings, how does a prolonged Middle East crisis affect the raw-material cost outlook: van den Broek puts the impact of the Middle East crisis at around 100 M€ of cost inflation concentrated in Asia and Africa, offset by cost savings 'one to three years ahead' on cross-functional and cross-market initiatives; specifies that the savings are 'reinvested to offset' inflation while maintaining pricing discipline and the 2%-6% guidance range.

dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: Operating income (beia) growth reiterated at +2% to +6% for FY2026; gross savings targeted at the high end of the 400-500 M€ range; effective tax rate ~28% (Costa Rica integration); other net finance charges 175-225 M€; average effective interest rate ~3,5%; capex <8% of net revenue; FIFCO/Costa Rica acquisition +2 to 3% accretive to EPS, buybacks +2% accretive to EPS.
pointsCles: Beia operating profit up 6.7% organically to EUR 2,170m with margin up 55bp to 14.6%, all regions contributing (AME +30.8%, APAC +17.7% leading); reported IFRS operating profit jumped 48.4% to EUR 2,126m, flattered by a EUR 473m one-off revaluation gain on the pre-held 25% stake in Heineken Costa Rica; net profit (beia) +10.2% organic to EUR 1,256m, diluted EPS (beia) EUR 2.29 (+11.6% constant currency) vs reported IFRS diluted EPS of EUR 2.05.

Growth quality driven by focus markets (>90% of the 2.6% organic net revenue growth: Vietnam, Ethiopia, Nigeria, India, Brazil, UK, France): total volume +1.6%, premium +5.8%, Heineken brand +5.3%, Heineken 0.0 +7.2%, Silver +34.5%; APAC standout (volume +11.6%, record Vietnam share, China portfolio ~+30% and a top-3 net profit contributor via the unconsolidated CRB partnership) while the Americas disappointed (volume -3.4%, share losses in Mexico/Brazil, management explicitly unsatisfied, recovery flagged for H2).

FIFCO/Heineken Costa Rica integration (EUR 2.9bn, closed 30 Jan 2026) ahead of plan and DRC exit (Bralima sold 10 Apr 2026) shift to asset-light licensing, together +2-3% EPS accretive in FY26; CEO transition in progress: Dolf van den Brink left 31 May 2026, Rafa Oliveira starts 1 Oct 2026, CFO Harold van den Broek hosted the call solo and stressed EverGreen 2030 continuity (~3,000 FTE reduction in H1, ~4,000-strong Heineken Business Services, four European multi-market organisations, 40+ innovation pilots).

Cash inflection is the standout: free operating cash flow of EUR 1.4bn vs EUR 257m in H1 25 (97% cash conversion, ~EUR 600m working-capital swing, capex down to 7.2% of net revenue vs 9.9%); net debt rose to EUR 17,675m on the Costa Rica funding, lifting net debt/EBITDA (beia) to 2.6x vs the <2.5x target with a return below target expected by year-end; interim dividend EUR 0.76 and the EUR 1.5bn buyback (~+2% EPS) continue.

hypothese.guidanceLongTerme: EverGreen 2030 (strategy unveiled at the end of 2025, execution accelerated since 2026): ambition of superior and balanced growth (volume/value), annual gross savings targeted at 400-500 M€, target of a net debt/EBITDA (beia) ratio durably below 2,5x, dividend policy widened to a range of 30% to 50% of net profit (beia, against 30-40% previously). No single quantified operating margin or revenue CAGR target out to 2030 identified in the sources consulted to date.
hypothese.summary: International premium brewer, controlled by the founding family through a dual-listed structure, which is accelerating its EverGreen 2030 plan (productivity + premiumisation + global brands) while digesting its largest acquisition in a decade (Costa Rica/FIFCO) - net debt rises temporarily but cash generation remains solid.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Heineken is the world's most international brewer, premium-positioned (Heineken, Amstel, Tiger, Birra Moretti, Desperados) and deliberately weighted toward high-potential emerging markets (Vietnam, India, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Brazil). The bet is EverGreen 2030 execution: accelerate organic growth via 18 priority markets and 5 global brands, funded by an ambitious productivity program (400-500M EUR gross savings/yr; 5,000-6,000 role reductions over two years). S1 26 confirms: total volume growing (+1.6%), all five global brands growing, beia operating margin +55bp in an environment management itself calls volatile - FY26 guidance (+2 to +6% beia operating profit) confirmed. The second pillar is governance: Heineken Holding (50%, family-controlled via L'Arche Green) - a long-horizon anchor shareholder. Near-term risks: net debt jumped to ~17bn EUR (2.6x beia EBITDA, above the <2.5x target) funding the FIFCO/Costa Rica acquisition (2.9bn EUR) - deleveraging is the proven post-deal playbook (Distell 2023) - and a CEO transition on 1 October 2026, the pivotal test of EverGreen continuity.

== THESIS READ ==
- FY26 beia guidance confirmed (+2-6%) with savings at the top of the range: the productivity engine is carrying the P&L while volumes heal.
- The 2026 EPS optics are inflated by the Costa Rica disposal gain (+473M EUR, ~+0.87 EUR/share, one-off): 2027 rebases lower by construction (4.32 -> 3.84 EUR) - a modeled cliff, not a deterioration.
- Net debt 2.6x post-FIFCO vs <2.5x target: the deleveraging glide (17.0 -> 11.5bn EUR modeled) is the balance-sheet thesis; the bridge carries the falling interest line explicitly.
- All five global brands growing and 80%+ of priority markets holding/gaining share - EverGreen's breadth test passes at mid-year.
- Watch: new CEO's first strategic communication (post 1 Oct) - continuity of EverGreen 2030 and of the savings cadence.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None (the Holding/NV dual structure is permanent governance, no valuePct).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: data.ebit = published IFRS operating profit; data starts in 2022 by documented choice (FY20 Covid impairments, FY21 UBL revaluation gain +1,270M - both regime-atypical, excluded rather than reconstructed); FY2024 net retreated per d-bis (+1,017M CR Beer impairment add-back, computation traced). Bridge (c-ter): tax 28% (ancrage), interest -630 -> -440M EUR with deleveraging, minorities -290M flat, and the beia-to-published WEDGE aggregated in 'other' (-604 -> -951M EUR; +106 in 2026 where the Costa Rica gain flips it) - explicitly a first-pass aggregate to decompose from the annual report (brand amortization, associates, exceptionals). omniumNet 2026 INCLUDES the +473M Costa Rica one-off; 2027 rebases on ~1,884M underlying then ~+9%/yr (FIFCO full-year accretion, buyback relution, EverGreen growth). Scorecard: beia-OP-guided house - FY26 anchor 4,560M EUR (initial +2-6% on 4,385 realized, sourced 11/02), metric mismatch declared, history to backfill, application suspended. WATCH-LIST: (1) deleveraging pace vs 2.5x; (2) new CEO communication; (3) Vietnam momentum through H2; (4) decompose the beia wedge at the FY26 annual report; (5) backfill FY24/25 initial beia guidance anchors. Next useful refresh: Q3 trading update (late October).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 trading update (late Oct); CEO transition (1 Oct) first signals; deleveraging trajectory; EverGreen 2030 margin cadence.

ancrages.moteur: Organic growth carried by the 18 priority markets (Vietnam, India, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Brazil to the fore) and the 5 global brands (Heineken®, Amstel, Tiger, Birra Moretti, Desperados, all growing in H1 26), amplified by the full-year consolidation of HEINEKEN Costa Rica from H2 26 - revenue built bottom-up (reported H1 26 + H2 estimate based on the operating income growth guidance and the FIFCO consolidation), then extended at a mid-single-digit growth rate over 2027-2030 consistent with the EverGreen 2030 framework (no quantified revenue target communicated by management).

Operating margin expansion carried by the EverGreen 2030 productivity programme (400-500 M€ of annual gross savings targeted, high end of the range in 2026), organisational simplification (MMOs, doubling of HEINEKEN Business Services, reduction of 5 000 to 6 000 positions over 2 years) and the premium/global brand mix - projection on the reported basis (IFRS, including the recurring noise of operating exceptional items year after year, not adjusted), medium confidence given the historical volatility of reported operating income (beia/reported gap of 979 to 1 214 M€/yr over 2023-2025, largely unpredictable from one year to the next).

One-off accounting gain, already recognised, of 473 M€ (tax-exempt) on the fair-value remeasurement of the 25% stake already held in HEINEKEN Costa Rica at the taking of control on 30 January 2026, included in the reported net income for H1 2026 - retained as such in omniumNet.2026 (impact ~+0,87€/share) but explicitly NOT carried forward into omniumNet.2027 and beyond, which restart from a normalised base excluding this gain (see text, METHODOLOGY section) so as not to compound it unduly over the projection horizon.

EPS accretion via two cumulative levers explicitly guided by management: ~+2 to 3% tied to the integration of FIFCO/Costa Rica (synergies, volume effect) and ~+2%/yr tied to the continuation of the 1,5 Md€ share buyback programme over 2 years (second tranche of 750 M€ under way, 380 M€ executed as at 31/07/2026) - diluted share count projected to decline continuously by roughly 1,5 to 2%/yr over the horizon, a plausible continuation given the observed pace (557 M at end-2025 -> 548,7 M weighted average in H1 26).

Elevated 2026 net debt (17 675 M€ at 30/06/2026, a ratio of 2,6x beia EBITDA) on account of the cash financing of the Costa Rica acquisition, progressive deleveraging expected over the projection horizon via free operating cash-flow (already markedly improved in H1 26, 1,4 Md€ vs 257 M€ in H1 25) and continued capital discipline, with a return targeted below the 2,5x long-term objective - a pattern analogous to the deleveraging observed after the Distell/Namibia Breweries acquisition (net debt 15 835 M€ at end-2023 -> 14 479 M€ at end-2025).

Normative tax rate taken at ~28%, consistent with management's explicit FY26 guidance (already raised vs 27,2% in 2025 on account of the tax integration of HEINEKEN Costa Rica), held stable over the projection horizon in the absence of any newly announced item.
